Intro

I am an engineering manager in Singapore, currently Vice President, Group Operations at a large bank in Singapore.

I lead a team of 7–8 engineers and data scientists in operational data, developing GenAI and agentic AI solutions for banking customers and internal users — including the transformation from GenAI solutions to agentic AI solutions — with a strong focus on evaluation, governance, and operational readiness in a regulated environment.

My focus is deployment engineering: architecture, evaluation, reliability, and adoption, rather than model research alone.

GenAI to agentic AI transformation

Developing GenAI and agentic AI solutions for banking customers and internal users, moving from GenAI solutions to agentic AI solutions in production, regulated workflows. Instead of one assistant that only answers, an orchestrator reads the user's query, works out the goal, and routes the work to specialised sub-agents that use data and tools to complete the task.

How the agentic system works

The pattern behind the first showcase, step by step. Select a stage to read what it does.

From a user's query to one combined answer

Each stage has its own job — and its own prompt that tells it how to do that job.

→ → → →

Orchestrator

Understands the user's input, breaks it into the tasks needed, and works out which sub-agents are required to generate the answer. Simple questions that need no knowledge-base information are answered directly here.

Prompt: the orchestrator has its own prompt, describing each sub-agent — what it is for, when to use it, and what it returns — so it can plan the work.

The sub-agents

Each sub-agent covers one broad area of banking help, so questions are handled in general terms. Select one to see what it handles.

Account Information. General help with account-related questions — for example, questions about accounts and the information or services connected to them.
